basics.name: Nischay Patel
basics.label: Computational biology researcher
basics.summary: Computational biology researcher applying statistical and machine-learning methods to single-cell, spatial, and transcriptomic data. My work includes representation-based cross-tissue comparison of cell states, latent-variable modeling of spatial cell-cell communication, and RNA-seq-based inference of gene-regulatory networks. I am interested in developing quantitative approaches to investigate genome regulation and disease mechanisms.

work.name: IIT Gandhinagar
work.title: DNA barcoding of Indian medicinal plants
work.summary: Developed nine DNA barcodes for Bougainvillea, Plumeria, and Dianthus using the matK marker, combining DNA extraction, primer design, PCR, Sanger sequencing, and phylogenetic analysis.
highlights: Extracted plant DNA using DNeasy Plant Kit and CTAB methods, and designed matK-specific M13-tagged primers.
Performed gradient PCR optimization, gel-electrophoresis validation, and Sanger sequencing of purified PCR products.
Conducted sequence trimming, manual base-calling, quality checks, BLAST database searches, and phylogenetic analysis.
Analyzed nine samples revealing approximately 1–2.7% genetic polymorphism in matK.

work.name: IIT Gandhinagar
work.title: Long non-coding RNAs in Arabidopsis pollination compatibility
work.summary: Designed an RNA-seq workflow for compatible and incompatible pollination in Arabidopsis, identifying 1,002 novel and 43 differentially expressed lncRNA loci and investigating potential regulatory interactions.
highlights: Analyzed 12 pollination samples across 10- and 60-minute time points using HISAT2 alignment, StringTie assembly, coding-potential tests, Kallisto quantification, and DESeq2.
Identified 1,002 novel and 43 differentially expressed lncRNA loci, revealing potential cis- and trans-lncRNA–mRNA interactions.
Constructed lncRNA–mRNA–miRNA networks using Spearman correlation, LncTar, psRNATarget, and Cytoscape.
Used GO analysis to investigate stress-defense responses, pollen–stigma recognition, and self-incompatibility pathways.

work.name: Tsinghua University · Amgen Scholars Program
work.title: Comparative single-cell analysis of ACP and tooth development
work.summary: Built a single-cell RNA-seq workflow for 32,000 adamantinomatous craniopharyngioma (ACP) tumor cells and developed a cross-tissue transfer-learning approach to compare tumor states with tooth-developmental reference atlases.
highlights: Integrated feature selection, PCA, clustering, and cell-type annotation for 32,000 ACP tumor cells.
Applied SCimilarity search using 128-dimensional triplet-loss embeddings trained on 23 million cells.
Developed a cross-tissue transfer-learning approach and identified tooth-related atlases as close matches for ACP tumor cells.
Used DESeq2 and GO enrichment to identify conserved WNT-signaling and morphogenesis pathways linking tumor states with odontogenic tissues.

projects.name: Differential cell-cell communication inference using spatial transcriptomics
highlights: Designed a multi-condition framework for differential cell-cell communication analysis from spatial transcriptomics data.
Adapted scDisInFact for ligand–receptor pairs to disentangle shared and cancer-specific features using latent-variable modeling.
Performed Mann–Whitney differential inference and model-based ΔLR scoring to quantify condition-driven changes.
Integrated spatial-proximity constraints through distance metrics and neighborhood embeddings.

projects.name: Reversal of sex-ratio distortion in a transgenic line of Aedes aegypti
projects.institution: Lab of Neural Systems, IIT Kanpur
highlights: Analyzed potential transcription-factor binding sites at a transgenic insertion site using JASPAR.
Performed protein–DNA docking simulations to assess potential disruption of doublesex (dsx) transcription-factor binding.
Analyzed sequence-specific binding interactions for potential changes in dsx isoforms involved in sexual differentiation.
Designed primers and performed PCR of CRISPR-Cas9 off-target regions potentially linked to sex-ratio distortion.

projects.name: Multimodal prediction of depression subtypes
highlights: Designed a multimodal machine-learning pipeline integrating audio, video, and transcripts to predict mental-health outcomes including PTSD and depression.
Generated summary statistics and temporal representations, with Whisper-based speech transcripts and BERT embeddings.
Applied mutual-information feature selection, PCA, and SMOTE.
Used SHAP, sentiment analysis, radar plots, and correlations to investigate modality-specific predictive signals.
Delivered seven lectures and tutorials on computational biology and bioinformatics tools and algorithms.
Led a team of 50 applying machine-learning approaches to biological datasets.
Represented the institute table-tennis team; received a silver medal and best-upcoming-player recognition at inter-institute tournaments.
Coordinated logistics and execution of institute sports events involving multiple teams.
